Kept as before/after evidence of our own behaviour and moved out of the reference store so no glob can reach it. Identified as ours by measurement rather than by filename: the renderer is ANGLE Metal naming an Apple M4 Max, so it ran on that Mac, yet it reports colorDepth 24 where every stock-Chrome capture of the same panel reports 30, timezone UTC where the machine is Asia/Bangkok, and 9 detected fonts against 32. anchor_exception.reason: This is the tree's only measurement of stock Chromium's own software rasteriser, and its identity strings are the rasteriser's own, so there is no hardware claim to misattribute. A host with no usable GPU device really does render through SwiftShader and without this anchor has no servable identity at all, which is worse for the user than a coherent software one. The allowance is for the GPU capability cluster of that one software backend and for nothing else: it cannot mint a persona block, because the decomposition gate refuses not-a-reference unconditionally, and it cannot mint a hardware anchor, because build-anchors requires the measured backend to equal the backend named here. Cited by patches 0027, 0038, 0052, 0091, 0102 and 0104. Clearing it needs a headed capture from a GPU-less Linux host on the current collector.

The GPU is physically present, so the GPU cluster is admissible and nothing else is. This is the case the endpoint discriminator CANNOT see: a cloud gaming host runs a full Windows install and reports {audioinput:1, audiooutput:1} and 33 font families, byte-identical in shape to the physical Singapore box. What separates it is the panel: screen 1975x1277 at dpr 1.75 is a streamed browser window scaled by the client, not a mode any display ships, and America/Los_Angeles is the service region rather than the user's desk. windows-nvidia-ampere-a4500-20260915T191.refuted_by: A shipped panel tuple at integer dpr would remove the only measured evidence for this tier and leave it resting on provenance alone.

discriminator.do_not_use_font_count: fonts.detected size is NOT a tier signal. It is platform- and collector-relative and it inverts inside one platform: linux-ws, a real workstation, detects 9 where the Berlin containers detect 11. The 3070 Ti and the A4500 both detect 33. Anyone reaching for it as a discriminator is reading a font-provisioning difference as a provenance one.
discriminator.stage_1_no_endpoints: media.devices counts EMPTY ({}) means a headless container. In this corpus it convicts the four Berlin linux-nvidia captures and nothing else; every installed desktop reports at least one endpoint. The test must be 'no endpoints at all', not 'has a microphone': the Sri Lanka desktop reports {videoinput, audiooutput} with no audioinput and is physical.
discriminator.stage_2_panel_tuple: A shipped display mode at integer devicePixelRatio. Convicts the A4500 (1975x1277 at dpr 1.75, a client-scaled stream) and independently re-convicts the four containers (1368x852, 2056x1290). Passes the Singapore 3070 Ti and Sri Lanka, both 1920x1080 at dpr 1. This is the load-bearing cloud-vs-physical signal, because stage 1 cannot see a cloud gaming host at all.

keys.anchor_exception: the one narrow use a not-a-reference capture is allowed, named with the backend it is allowed for
keys.device: stable id of the physical thing measured, so two captures of one machine are visibly one machine
keys.justification: the measurement that supports the tier
keys.refuted_by: what would have to be observed for the tier to be wrong
keys.sha256: sha256 of the capture bytes; the lookup key. A capture whose bytes no longer match its entry fails closed.
keys.superseded_by: a capture of the SAME device on a newer collector. The older capture's recorded values remain valid evidence for the surfaces they were read for; what the field says is that the corpus should not mint blocks from both halves of one device. Recorded, not enforced.
keys.tier: one of the three tiers above

purpose: What each capture IS, recorded explicitly because it cannot be derived. A tier is a claim about the world — whether a machine is a desk or a hypervisor — and no probe answers it. Filenames and labels are descriptive and decide nothing, so each entry carries the measurement that supports its tier and what would have to be observed to refute it.

read_by.capture/derive/conform.py: refuses a reference tiered not-a-reference, because holding our own browser to its own output proves only that we agree with ourselves, and refuses a capture with no entry here at all: absence of a claim is not a weak claim, it is none
read_by.not enforced anywhere: physical-gpu-only, superseded_by and the not-a-reference tier are NOT gates on block decomposition or profile composition. The generation-aware relaxation of the decomposition gate that would have used them was dropped as disproportionate: a gate that blocks a reasonable composition is worse than the labelling imprecision it prevents. They are recorded here so a reader citing a capture as evidence can look up what it is, which is the part that was missing.
read_by.scripts/build-anchors.py: an anchor may be built from a capture with no accepted admission record only when this file records an anchor_exception whose backend equals the backend measured in that capture

tiers.not-a-reference: Our own browser's output, or a session with automation suspicion. May never mint a block and may never be the reference side of a conformance run.
tiers.physical-full: An installed physical machine someone uses. Trustworthy for every cluster: platform, gpu, display, hardware, locale and theme.
tiers.physical-gpu-only: A virtual machine with a real passthrough GPU. The GPU capability cluster is a true measurement of silicon that is physically present; every other cluster is a hypervisor artifact. Admissible for the gpu block alone.
